Methods for Skellam Regression Fits

Source: R/skellam.reg.R
skellam_reg-methods.Rd

Extractor, prediction and testing methods for objects returned by skellam.reg.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'skellam_reg'
print(x, digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L), ...)

# S3 method for class 'skellam_reg'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'skellam_reg'
coef(object, model = c("full", "lambda1", "lambda2"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'skellam_reg'
vcov(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'skellam_reg'
logLik(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'skellam_reg'
nobs(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'skellam_reg'
fitted(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'skellam_reg'
residuals(object, type = c("response", "pearson", "quantile"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'skellam_reg'
predict(
  object,
  newdata = NULL,
  type = c("response", "lambda1", "lambda2", "rates", "prob", "cdf"),
  at = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'skellam_reg'
simulate(object, nsim = 1, seed = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'skellam_reg'
anova(object, ...)

Arguments

digits

Number of significant digits to print.

...

Further fitted models (for anova); otherwise unused.

object, x

A "skellam_reg" object.

model

For coef: "full" (all coefficients, named lambda1:... and lambda2:...), "lambda1" or "lambda2".

type

For predict: "response" (the fitted mean \(\lambda_1 - \lambda_2\)), "lambda1", "lambda2", "rates" (both), "prob" (the probabilities of the values in at) or "cdf". For residuals: "response" (\(y - (\lambda_1 - \lambda_2)\)), "pearson" (divided by \(\sqrt{\lambda_1 + \lambda_2}\)) or "quantile" (randomized quantile residuals, Dunn and Smyth 1996, standard normal when the model is right; they use random numbers).

newdata

Optional data frame for predict; if omitted, the fitted values are used.

at

Integer values at which type = "prob" or "cdf" are evaluated; one column per value.

nsim, seed

As in simulate.

Value

coef, vcov, logLik, nobs, fitted and residuals return what their names say; predict returns a vector, or a matrix for type = "rates", "prob" and "cdf"; simulate a data frame of simulated responses; anova a likelihood-ratio test table for nested models.

References

Dunn, P. K. and Smyth, G. K. (1996) Randomized quantile residuals. Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics 5(3), 236-244.
